fields.meta_description: Build a workshop registration form that holds seats per session and emails each registrant the supply list or setup steps their answers call for.
fields.h1: Build a Workshop Registration Form for Hands-On Classes
fields.hero_description: Build a workshop registration form that caps each session's seats and saves every sign-up to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What Each Registrant Answers, and Where It Goes
fields.features_subheading: Before the first session, an instructor needs a headcount and a supply list. Each piece below collects part of that at sign-up.
fields.feature_1:
A seat limit on every session

Give each date and time its own seat count, such as 10 benches or 16 cooking stations. When a session fills, the form takes it off the list and the others stay open.
fields.feature_2:
Session choices that follow experience

Ask whether the registrant has done this kind of work before. Anyone who answers no sees only the beginner session, and the advanced one appears for people who answer yes.
fields.feature_3:
The right supply list in each confirmation

Write one list per option, such as laptop setup for Mac and another for Windows. The app emails each registrant the list that matches their answers as soon as they submit.
fields.feature_4:
Dietary needs counted before class

Ask each registrant about dietary needs once. The morning before the session, the host gets an email with a count for each need and the names of the people behind it.
fields.feature_5:
A roster for each session

Each registration saves as a row in a database you own. A dashboard groups the rows by session with every answer beside the name, and the instructor checks people in from it.
fields.feature_6:
Code that moves to your GitHub

On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository. A developer can restyle the emails, add a field the form lacks, or run it beside the rest of your class catalog.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Workshops and What Each Form Asks
fields.tab_content_1:
With no saw experience, Florentyna gets Shop Basics

Gorsemoor Makerspace splits its cutting board workshop into two Saturday sessions: Shop Basics at 9:00 AM and Open Build at 1:00 PM. The form asks each registrant whether they have used a table saw. Florentyna Ledoux answers no, so the form offers her only Shop Basics, and she takes bench 7 of 10.
fields.tab_content_2:
Mac or Windows decides which setup email goes out

Everyone who registers for the Intro to Python workshop at Tidewick Public Library says which laptop they will bring. Of 22 registrants, 13 chose Mac and 9 chose Windows. Each confirmation email carries the install steps for that machine. Cosimo Cobbett picked Windows, and his email lists the Windows steps.
fields.tab_content_3:
For 16 cooks, one email sets the chef's prep list

Sallowfield Kitchen seats 16 cooks at its fresh pasta class and asks each one about dietary needs. The morning before class, chef Rosamund Drummore gets an email with the counts: 11 with no needs, 3 vegetarian, and 2 gluten-free. She plans the fillings and the gluten-free dough from that one email.
fields.tab_content_4:
Once all 8 kits are reserved, Eulalie gets a supply list

Watercolor students at Brightlane Art Studio can borrow a paint kit for the 4-week workshop, and the studio owns 8. When the 8th kit is reserved, the form hides the kit option. Eulalie Marchetti-Fry registers next and gets the bring-your-own supply list in her confirmation email.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Workshop Registration Form
fields.howto_description: Follow these seven steps to build a workshop registration form that seats each person in the right session and says what to bring.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Count the seats in each session
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Write a supply list for every option
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Ask about diets when food is served
fields.howto_step_1_des: List every date and start time with its own seat count. A woodshop might have 10 benches and a kitchen 16 stations. The form closes each session on its own when it reaches that number, while the others keep taking registrations.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Write one question a beginner can answer honestly, such as whether they have run a lathe or written code before. Then decide which sessions each answer opens, and keep the advanced session hidden from anyone who answers no.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Write a separate list for each choice a registrant can make: Mac setup and Windows setup, or a loaner kit and a bring-your-own list. Each confirmation email then carries only the list that matches the answers on that registration.
fields.howto_step_4_des: If the workshop serves lunch or cooks something, ask about dietary needs as a short list of choices with an Other box. Pick who receives the counts, such as the chef or the caterer, and how long before the session they arrive.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Tell Emergent how the workshop runs
fields.howto_step_5_des: Describe the workshop to Emergent in plain English: the sessions with their seats, plus the questions and the email each answer triggers. From that description Emergent builds the form with its database, and you change any part later by prompting.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Sign up twice with test addresses
fields.howto_step_6_des: Register once as a beginner and once as someone with experience. Check that each sees the right sessions and that each confirmation email carries the right supply list. Fix any wording that reads wrong before the link goes out.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Share the link and set a close date
fields.howto_step_7_des: Post the link where your students already look, such as your class calendar or newsletter. Close sign-ups a few days before the first session. That leaves time to order materials for the final headcount and set up the room.

faq_plan.q: What is a workshop registration form?
faq_plan.a: A workshop registration form is how people sign up for a workshop, which the Oxford Learner's Dictionaries describe as a period of discussion and practical work on a particular subject. Because the work is practical, the form asks for more than a name and email: which session, and what experience or equipment the person brings.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a workshop registration form?
faq_plan.a: List your sessions and their seat counts, decide what each registrant must tell you, and write the confirmation email. Then describe all of it in a prompt to Emergent's AI form builder, which builds the form and the database the registrations save to. Test it with two sign-ups before you share the link.

faq_plan.q: Is a seminar registration form different from a workshop form?
faq_plan.a: Yes, mostly in the questions it asks. Oxford's learner dictionary defines a seminar as a meeting for discussion or training, while a workshop adds practical work. A seminar registration form can stop at contact details and a session choice. Give a workshop form questions about experience and supplies, because attendees do the work in the room.

faq_plan.q: What fields belong in a workshop registration form template?
faq_plan.a: Start with contact details and the session date, then add what the hands-on part needs: experience level, equipment, dietary needs, and an accessibility note. A workshop registration form template that stops at contact details leaves the instructor emailing everyone later. For a multi-day event with tracks and badges, a conference registration form fits better.

faq_plan.q: How do I limit seats per session on a workshop registration form?
faq_plan.a: Set a seat count on each session rather than on the workshop as a whole, and base it on the scarcest thing in the room, such as benches or loaner kits. If registrants email back a PDF workshop registration form, someone has to count the seats by hand. Forms built with Emergent have no response caps.

faq_plan.q: What should the confirmation email from a workshop registration form include?
faq_plan.a: Include the session name, date, start time, and address, plus what to bring, matched to the person's answers. Add parking or entry directions if the venue is hard to find, and a contact for questions. Send a reminder a day or two before with the same details.

faq_plan.q: What should a workshop registration form for kids ask parents?
faq_plan.a: Ask the parent or guardian for their contact details, plus the child's name and age to place the child in the right group. Add who may pick the child up, and dietary needs if snacks are served. For ongoing care rather than a one-time class, use a daycare registration form instead.

faq_plan.q: When should a workshop registration form stop taking sign-ups?
faq_plan.a: Close it when you need a final headcount to buy materials, such as 3 days before a class that uses fresh ingredients. Set the close date on the form itself. A late visitor then sees that sign-ups have ended, not a form that still accepts them.

faq_plan.q: Can one workshop registration form cover every session in a series?
faq_plan.a: Yes. List every session in the series on one form and let each person tick the dates they will attend, or offer the full series as a single choice. Each choice saves with the registration, and the instructor sees who is coming to each date. Emergent builds the form and its dashboard from a description of the series.

faq_plan.q: How can a workshop registration form help with check-in at the door?
faq_plan.a: Use the registrations as your check-in list. Each sign-up is a row, and the instructor opens that session's list at the door to tick off names as people arrive. The same approach works with a registration form for any event, such as a talk or a club meeting. With an app built on Emergent, those rows live in a database you own.

plan.angle: The top 10 is template galleries (SurveyMonkey, Jotform, 123FormBuilder, Wufoo, Formsite, AidaForm), a printable template and two blog posts. Each template stops at name, email and a session dropdown. This page shows what a hands-on workshop needs once people sign up: a makerspace that offers beginners only its intro session, a library coding class that emails Mac and Windows setup steps by answer, a cooking studio whose chef gets dietary counts the morning before, and a painting studio whose form drops the loaner-kit option once all 8 kits are reserved. The FAQ covers the definition, building one, seminar versus workshop forms, template fields, per-session seat limits, the confirmation email, children's workshops, when to close sign-ups, multi-session series, and day-of check-in.
